alternative: This alternative uses a known difference between the two models and the generic shape of gradient updates. Every fine-tune of this base gets updates of the form sum(delta x^T). Its right (input) singular vectors therefore lean toward the input directions that the base's own activations drive hard. RL-Math 3.1's top-8 input directions are such directions: the base's text drives them 8-11x more than random (result-a7c052), and they sit 1.33x inside the base matrix's own top input subspace (result-3abd6f). So any change, Think-SFT's included, gets an input-side capture above chance for free. That is the 4.80x-chance cap_right of Think-SFT (F27), which is also 2.0-2.2x the IF and General subspaces. The output (left) side carries the loss-specific write. Math 3.0 has the same math reward as Math 3.1 and a concentrated update (top-8 share 0.135), so it shares Math 3.1's input-output pairs and captures on both sides. Think-SFT's update is diffuse (top-8 share 0.030, result-82eb02) and imitation-driven, so it writes along RL-Math's output directions only at about chance. If cap_left_TS is about 8/d_out and cap_right_TS is about 4.8 x 8/d_in, then r_TS is about d_in/(4.8 d_out). Math 3.0 has r_M30 = (a_L/a_R)(d_in/d_out) with comparable excess multiples a_L and a_R. So q is about (1/4.8)(a_R/a_L), roughly 0.2-0.3, well inside [0.05, 0.7]. The prediction needs nothing beyond 'input capture is generic and output capture is reward-specific', plus Think-SFT's known diffuseness.
computation: 1) From studies/theory/data/direct_host/cap_v1.json, for each of the 224 matrices read d_out and d_in from the matrix shape (q,k,v,o 4096x4096; gate,up 11008x4096; down 4096x11008, or as the file records them). Also read cap_right_TS, cap_left_M30 and cap_right_M30 against the Math 3.1 top-8 entry. Do NOT read cap_left_TS. 2) Replace Think-SFT's output-side capture with its chance level: cap_left_TS_alt = 8/d_out. 3) Compute r_TS_alt = (8/d_out) / cap_right_TS and r_M30 = cap_left_M30 / cap_right_M30. 4) Compute q_alt = r_TS_alt / r_M30 per matrix. 5) Q_alt = median of q_alt over the 224 matrices. Q_alt is on the statistic's scale. Expected about 0.25: with cap_right_TS about 4.8x chance and Math 3.0's left and right excess multiples comparable, q_alt is about 1/4.8 times (a_R/a_L).
